Blends above E10 require approvals and some specialized equipment to meet the patchwork of regulations that cover refueling infrastructure (Section 2.6.5). Stations interested in selling ethanol blends can refer to Clean Cities’ Handbook for Handling, Storing, and Dispensing E85 and Other Ethanol-Gasoline Blends, which explains requirements for selling ethanol blends and provides lists of compatible and UL-listed equipment (DOE 2016).15 As of the end of 2024, E85 was available at 4,717 stations in 43 states (Figure 32) (Alternative Fuels Data Center 2025c). As of July 2025, there were 4,300 stations in 34 states selling E15 (Growth Energy 2025). Model year 2001 and newer light-duty trucks and vehicles are approved by EPA to operate on E15 (EPA 2026). At the end of 2024, 97% of the gasoline light-duty truck and vehicle population was model year 2001 and newer.16 Flexible-fuel vehicles can operate on any gasoline-ethanol blended fuel between E0 and E85, and there were nearly 20 million flexible-fuel vehicles on U.S. roads at the end of 2024. There were 42 models from six manufacturers in model year 2017, but only four models offered from two manufacturers in model year 2023. The reason for the decline was a change to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration’s Corporate Average Fuel Economy standards, in which auto manufacturers receive a credit for flexible-fuel vehicles sold. For model year 2020 and beyond, auto manufacturers must demonstrate that the vehicle is using E85 to obtain credits, which has led to a steep decline in the availability of flexible-fuel vehicles. 2.8 Renewable Natural Gas RNG, or biomethane, is a pipeline-quality gas that is interchangeable with conventional natural gas and thus can be used in natural gas vehicles and other applications. RNG is essentially biogas (the gaseous product of the decomposition of organic matter, composed primarily of methane, carbon dioxide, and other trace compounds) that has been processed to purity standards. Like conventional natural gas, RNG can be used as a transportation fuel in the form of compressed natural gas or liquefied natural gas. RNG qualifies as a cellulosic biofuel
